headline: Southborough boards revised the regional school budget, benchmarked municipal employee pay scales, and advanced draft zoning rules for senior housing.
synopsis: The Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee re-voted a revised $31.52 million FY27 budget, slightly reducing Southborough's assessment due to increased state Chapter 70 aid. The Personnel Board voted to adopt a 60th percentile salary benchmark for non-union town staff while establishing a November 24 deadline for employee job-classification appeals. Meanwhile, the Affordable Housing Trust backed a draft zoning bylaw permitting higher-density 55-plus housing and arranged to transfer one million dollars in trust funds into an interest-bearing account. In other business, committees prepared for upcoming trail grants and promoted the town's resident satisfaction survey ahead of a November phone system cutover.

highlights.title: Regional school budget re-voted with reduced town assessment
highlights.why: The regional school committee approved a revised $31.52 million budget that applies additional state Chapter 70 aid to lower Southborough's assessment to $10,731,901.

highlights.title: Personnel Board benchmarks town pay study to 60th percentile
highlights.why: The board voted to benchmark municipal salaries to the 60th percentile of comparable towns and established a review panel for staff appeals.

highlights.title: Draft senior housing zoning bylaw advanced
highlights.why: The trust endorsed a draft bylaw allowing up to eight units per acre on two-acre lots with a 12.5 percent affordable requirement, lifting the town's 7 percent elderly cap.

highlights.title: Housing trust funds moved to interest-bearing account
highlights.why: Approximately $1 million held in a non-interest account was transferred to an insured program yielding roughly 3.5 percent to earn an estimated $35,000 annually.

highlights.title: Outreach launched for 2027 MassTrails grant
highlights.why: The committee began preparatory outreach to schools and regional partners for a state trail grant offering up to $100,000 with a 20 percent town match.

highlights.title: Promotion planned for resident satisfaction survey
highlights.why: The committee coordinated outreach at polling places and through schools for the town survey, which covers municipal services and commercial drone sentiment.
